I farm the way I have done for years: I start from what I used last year, then I look at what the better fields around me are doing. On 10.1 mu, I cannot play games with yield. If wheat or maize goes thin, that loss hurts more than spending a little extra on fertilizer, so I will feed the crop a bit on the safe side and use my well when the ground turns dry. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed because the old kinds do not fill the ear as well now. I will rotary till after maize, put most of the phosphate in at sowing, give nitrogen in base and topdressing, and water about 3 times if the season is normal. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people here, keep the stubble work simple so I do not lose time after wheat harvest, put enough nitrogen because maize eats fertilizer fast, and water 2 times if rain is short. I do not like wasting money, but I dislike cutting fertilizer too hard even more, because one bad harvest is worse than a few extra bags.
